findings.title: test
findings.text: This test does not actually pin the temp-file+rename mechanism it is named for: a plain `std::fs::write` to a path that is a directory also fails with EISDIR (exit 3) and leaves the directory as the only entry, satisfying every assertion here. The success test likewise passes for a direct write (one file, no leftovers), and the unwritable-parent test also fails the same way. So replacing `write_manifest_atomically` with an in-place write would not fail any test in this file — the feature's core guarantee (a refusal or partial write leaves the existing target intact) is mutation-unprotected. Add a case that distinguishes the two implementations, e.g. a symlink target (a plain write follows it and clobbers the linked file, while staging+rename replaces the link) or an existing read-only target that can be renamed over but not opened for writing, and assert the pre-existing bytes survive.

findings.title: test
findings.text: Only the UNVERIFIABLE refusal (exit 3, absent decision log) is exercised with `--out`. The third outcome, FAIL (exit 1), is also a refusal that must leave the target untouched — a tampered `decisions/*.yml` returns 1 from the `Chain::Tampered` arm before the write. That direction is not covered here, so "write only on success" is not pinned for FAIL. Add a case that seeds a tampered decision record (as `tests/baseline.rs::emitting_refuses_a_tampered_decision_log` does), runs with `--out` over a seeded target, and asserts exit 1 plus unchanged target bytes.

findings.title: bug
findings.text: The success hint embeds the raw `--out` path inside a copy-pasteable shell command. For a path with a space or shell metacharacter (e.g. `--out 'my baselines/release.json'`), the printed line becomes `minisign -Sm my baselines/release.json`, so the operator following the instruction signs the wrong argument or gets a usage error. Print the path separately (it is already in the `wrote {out}` part) instead of splicing it into the command, or shell-quote it.

findings.title: documentation
findings.text: This change updates the inline usage string (here) and `BASELINE_HELP` in `src/main.rs`, but `run`'s own doc comment was left describing the pre-`--out` contract: the signature line still reads `req baseline --at <ts> [--verify <file>] ...` (no `--out`) and the next paragraph says "With no `--verify`, prints the canonical manifest to stdout" — no longer true when `--out` is given. Its `Exit:` summary also omits that a failed `--out` write reports `3`. Since the fn is `pub`, update the rustdoc alongside the usage string and main.rs help.

findings.title: bug
findings.text: `--out` does not create the target's parent directory, and `req init` scaffolds `claims/` and `aliases/` but not `baselines/`. So the documented invocation (`docs/adopting.md`: `req baseline --at "$(date -u ...)" --out baselines/release.json`) fails on a fresh corpus with exit 3 (`cannot write ... No such file or directory`) until the operator manually runs `mkdir -p baselines`. The missing-dir case is asserted as intended in `tests/baseline_out.rs`, so if auto-creating the parent is unwanted, the docs example needs the `mkdir` step; otherwise create the directory here (as the staging-dir path does).
